attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter. The following quote from The Information is support for his point, not the claim itself.

semantics.note: The normalised proposition matches his categorical claim that OpenAI and its peers have no plan beyond revenue growth. He stresses he is 'being quite literal', which supports treating it as an observation rather than pure rhetoric.

contract.note: The plain reading fits his literal framing: any concrete plan on cost or capital beyond revenue growth would refute it. The contract tests whether a plan exists, not whether it is credible, so his doubts about its sufficiency are not penalised. 'Make this work' is somewhat vague, but the reading is ordinary.

evidence.note: OpenAI CFO post dated 2026-01-18, before publication. It describes managing compute as a portfolio and serving workloads on lower-cost infrastructure for efficiency. That is a stated cost strategy beyond revenue growth. It is a company disclosure, but the claim is about whether a plan exists, and this post states one.

reviews.rationale: Before the post, OpenAI's CFO publicly set out efficiency measures, such as running high-volume workloads on cheaper hardware and actively managing compute. That goes beyond simply projecting more revenue. Revenue growth is still at the centre of OpenAI's plan, which partly matches Zitron's point, but his categorical 'neither... any plan' does not hold. Whether the plan is credible or sufficient is not assessed.

attribution.note: Zitron's own aside in his own newsletter.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps 'appears'. It is read as a claim about what the public record showed, not as a probability hedge, so it is treated as an observation.

contract.note: The result depends on what 'available' means: operationally deployed, or authorised by agreement. Zitron did not say which. OpenAI's classified-deployment agreement was announced before the snapshot date. If an agreement counts as availability, the claim fails; if only operational use counts, it may hold.

evidence.note: CNN on Feb 24 reports Claude was then the only model in Pentagon classified systems, and that xAI had signed a deal. This predates the March 2 snapshot, so it is context only.
OpenAI disclosure dated Feb 27-28 announcing an agreement to deploy in classified environments. It gives no operational start date, so it does not settle availability on March 2.

reviews.rationale: Claude's operational exclusivity is documented only for Feb 24. By March 2, OpenAI (and reportedly xAI) had classified-deployment agreements, but no evidence in the packet says whether either was operational by the snapshot date. Under the operational reading the claim may hold; under the authorisation reading it is doubtful. The packet does not settle it.
